aiProducts.title: PortfolioIQ
aiProducts.subtitle: A fully deployed Streamlit application demonstrating enterprise AI governance in action.
aiProducts.summary: A fully deployed, 6-screen Streamlit application demonstrating a Centaur governance model for enterprise application portfolio rationalization. Built to demonstrate enterprise AI product thinking beyond a simple chatbot, with governance, explainability, cost management, and human oversight built into the workflow.
capabilities: Explainable AI recommendation engine with 7-signal scoring
Jagged Frontier classification (a framework identifying where AI performs reliably versus where human judgment is essential): Inside, Edge, or Outside
Conversational semantic search powered by Claude
Per-session API governance with call limits
Access-controlled AI features with password gate
Live ServiceNow REST API with CSV fallback auto-detection
artifacts: Live deployed application on Streamlit Community Cloud
aiProducts.architectureNote: Deliberate choices: context stuffing over vector DB for explainability at current scale; direct Claude API over LangChain for transparency and control. Roadmap documents exactly when and why each would change at scale.
businessValue: Demonstrates AI product thinking beyond output generation, with governance, explainability, and human oversight built into every workflow
Includes 0→500 customer productization roadmap showing scaling strategy
Rapid end-to-end delivery demonstrates the ability to move quickly from concept to working software.
aiProducts.businessProblem: Enterprise application portfolios routinely include hundreds of systems, and retain, retire, or modernize decisions are often made on incomplete information or institutional memory rather than consistent, defensible criteria. Without structured decision support, organizations either move too slowly or make costly modernization mistakes.
aiProducts.productVision: The opportunity was to bring the same governance discipline used in the GE Vernova APM Dashboard to an AI-assisted version, one where AI accelerates the recommendation without removing human accountability for the decision.
aiProducts.technicalArchitecture: A governed decision-support architecture: enterprise portfolio data feeds a scoring and recommendation layer, every recommendation is explainable and routed through human review before any action is taken, and every decision is logged for auditability.
keyFeatures: Six-screen guided workflow from data intake to executive-ready recommendation
Accept, override, or escalate on every AI recommendation, with rationale required for overrides
Session-level governance controls to manage API usage responsibly
Exportable outputs designed for stakeholder and leadership review
aiProducts.blueprintConnection: PortfolioIQ demonstrates governance, executive decision support, and value realization, the same disciplines the Blueprint treats as inseparable, applied here to AI-assisted portfolio decisions specifically.

aiProducts.title: AI Security Triage Dashboard
aiProducts.subtitle: Enterprise threat and vulnerability decision-support with human-in-the-loop governance.
aiProducts.summary: A governed AI decision-support tool that helps security analysts triage CVE vulnerabilities, phishing emails, and active URL threat indicators. Built with the same governance architecture as the Portfolio Rationalization Advisor - AI generates a triage summary and recommended action, the analyst approves or overrides before anything executes, and every decision is logged with a full audit trail.
capabilities: CISA KEV cross-reference -  live exploitation status overlaid on every CVE, separating theoretical severity from operational priority.
Live CVE feed from NIST NVD API with CVSS severity scoring and AI triage summaries

Phishing email analysis using a labeled research corpus to demonstrate AI risk scoring, explainable recommendations, and triage workflow governance. The architecture is designed to integrate with enterprise email security gateways in production deployments.
URL threat indicator feed with severity classification and AI-generated mitigation recommendations
Human-in-the-loop review queue - no action executes without analyst approval
Override tracking - written rationale required before any AI recommendation is overridden
Full audit log across all three data sources with CSV export
Bounded agentic routing - AI recommends, human approves, system executes and logs
artifacts: Live deployed application on Streamlit Community Cloud
aiProducts.architectureNote: Same governance pattern applied to a cybersecurity context: retrieve threat data across multiple sources, AI reasons and recommends, human reviews before action executes, full audit log captures every decision. Demonstrates pattern reusability across domains. Built in response to identifying a cybersecurity domain gap - designed, built, and deployed in under 48 hours.
businessValue: Addresses analyst triage consistency — AI surfaces relevant threat context so every analyst makes decisions from the same information baseline
Override tracking identifies where AI and human judgment diverge, enabling continuous model improvement without retraining
Demonstrates governance-first AI PM thinking applied to a new domain under time pressure
aiProducts.businessProblem: Security analysts face a constant volume of CVEs, phishing reports, and threat indicators, more than can be manually triaged with consistent judgment. Inconsistent triage means real threats get buried under noise, and different analysts reach different conclusions from the same data.
aiProducts.productVision: The opportunity was to apply the same governed AI pattern used in portfolio decisions to a different domain under real time pressure, testing whether the governance model generalizes rather than being specific to one use case.
aiProducts.technicalArchitecture: A shared governance pattern applied to security operations: live threat data is retrieved from multiple sources, AI generates a triage recommendation, an analyst reviews and approves before anything executes, and every decision is captured in an audit trail.
keyFeatures: Unified triage view across CVEs, phishing reports, and URL threat indicators
Live exploitation status overlaid on every vulnerability, not just theoretical severity
Required written rationale before overriding any AI recommendation
Full exportable audit log across all three data sources
aiProducts.blueprintConnection: The Security Triage Dashboard demonstrates operational governance, the same human-in-the-loop, audit-first pattern proven on portfolio decisions, applied to a different domain to test whether the governance model actually generalizes.

aiProducts.title: Semantic CMDB Search Tool
aiProducts.subtitle: Natural-language search across ServiceNow CMDB records
aiProducts.summary: A working semantic search prototype connecting to a ServiceNow PDI via REST APIs, generating embeddings with OpenAI, and storing them in ChromaDB to enable natural-language search across CMDB records, surfacing system relationships, dependencies, and infrastructure context.
capabilities: Live ServiceNow PDI connection via REST API
Highlights CMDB data quality impact on retrieval accuracy
artifacts: Working local prototype with end-to-end retrieval pipeline
businessValue: Reduces time navigating complex system relationships
Surfaces dependencies and infrastructure context faster
Demonstrates real-world constraints of CMDB data quality on AI retrieval
aiProducts.businessProblem: Enterprise CMDB systems hold critical information about system dependencies and infrastructure relationships, but keyword search fails when people don't know the exact naming conventions or system IDs, so valuable context routinely goes unfound.
aiProducts.productVision: The opportunity was to test whether natural-language search could make an existing CMDB investment more usable, without replacing or duplicating the system of record.
aiProducts.technicalArchitecture: A retrieval-based architecture: enterprise CMDB data is indexed for semantic search, and natural-language queries return relevant system relationships and context rather than exact keyword matches.
keyFeatures: Natural-language query interface, no exact system names required
Surfaces system relationships and dependencies, not just matching records
Live connection to a ServiceNow instance via REST API
aiProducts.blueprintConnection: Semantic CMDB Search demonstrates organizational knowledge and AI-enabled discovery, making information the organization already has actually findable, one of the readiness gaps the Blueprint asks organizations to assess before scaling AI further.

aiProducts.title: AI Benefits Cost & Utilization Analyzer
aiProducts.subtitle: Decision-support for benefits and claims data analysis
aiProducts.imageAlt: AI Benefits Cost & Utilization Analyzer screenshot
aiProducts.summary: A decision-support prototype analyzing benefits and claims data for cost and utilization insights. Built on a Bronze-layer Data Lakehouse using open datasets (CMS, BLS, Medicare), with a roadmap including predictive analytics, document intelligence, and conversational interfaces.
capabilities: Bronze-layer Data Lakehouse using CMS, BLS, and Medicare datasets
Roadmap for predictive modeling and document intelligence
Strict data privacy and governance model
artifacts: Local prototype with ingestion pipeline and analytics layer
businessValue: Improves cost visibility for HR and finance stakeholders
Roadmap shows path to conversational interface and HR system integration
aiProducts.businessProblem: HR and finance stakeholders need visibility into benefits cost and utilization trends, but the underlying data is often fragmented across sources and requires significant manual work to turn into a usable view.
aiProducts.productVision: The opportunity was to demonstrate an enterprise data architecture, ingestion through analytics, that could support cost visibility today and predictive, conversational capabilities as the roadmap matures.
aiProducts.technicalArchitecture: A layered data architecture: benefits and claims data is ingested into a structured analytics layer, enabling cost and utilization analysis with a clear path toward predictive and conversational capabilities.
keyFeatures: Cost and utilization trend views built from real public benefits datasets
Structured, layered data pipeline built for future scale
Roadmap toward predictive modeling and a conversational interface
aiProducts.blueprintConnection: The Benefits Analyzer demonstrates enterprise data architecture thinking, building the data foundation a capability needs before adding predictive or conversational features on top of it, the same sequencing discipline behind the Blueprint's Capability Gaps phase.

enterpriseProjects.title: Application Portfolio Management (APM) Dashboard
enterpriseProjects.objective: Give leadership actionable visibility into the enterprise application portfolio to support investment, modernization, and retirement decisions.
enterpriseProjects.role: Application Portfolio Manager / Technical Product Manager
bullets: Identified a gap in leadership visibility into application health, cost, and risk across a 200+ application portfolio.
Defined the data model, decision framework, and success metrics that shaped what the dashboard measured and how decisions would be made from it.
Built and maintained the dashboard, consolidating health scores, technical debt, cost, and cloud adoption data into a single view.
Drove quarterly portfolio reviews with the CIO and business leaders, translating data into actionable recommendations for investment, retirement, or remediation.
Dashboard became the primary tool for portfolio decisions, enabling reduction of legacy systems, improved cloud adoption, and measurable cost savings.

sqdc.safety: Identified high-risk applications early before they became operational issues
sqdc.quality: Prioritized improvements based on data rather than opinion
sqdc.delivery: Established a predictable quarterly portfolio review cadence
sqdc.cost: Reduced maintenance spend and optimized investment allocation

enterpriseProjects.challenge: Leadership had no consolidated way to see application health, cost, and risk across a 200+ application portfolio.
outcomes: 50% improvement in application portfolio health scores
40% reduction in portfolio size through rationalization
Became the primary tool for quarterly CIO and Director portfolio reviews
enterpriseProjects.executiveSummary: GE Vernova needed to make application investment decisions on evidence rather than opinion, across a global portfolio of more than 200 applications. This initiative built the decision-support system that made that possible, and it became the mechanism through which CIOs and Directors actually made retain, retire, and modernize calls.
enterpriseProjects.businessChallenge: The portfolio had grown organically for years with no consistent way to compare applications on health, cost, or risk. Directors and CIOs were making high-stakes modernization and retirement decisions largely on institutional memory rather than structured data, with no shared definition across the organization of what "healthy" or "at risk" actually meant.
enterpriseProjects.myRole: I owned the dashboard end to end, from defining the decision framework it was built to support through to the data model, scoring approach, and the recurring executive review cadence that put it to use. The work was less about building a tool and more about designing the decision itself: what leadership needed to see, in what order, and what action each view was meant to drive.
keyContributions: Defined the data model, decision framework, and success metrics that shaped what the dashboard measured and how decisions got made from it.
Consolidated health scores, technical debt, cost, and cloud adoption data into a single executive view.
Established a quarterly portfolio review cadence directly with the CIO and business leaders.
enterpriseProjects.blueprintConnection: This is where the idea that AI recommendations need a decision framework before they need a model took shape. The dashboard only worked because the decision criteria existed before the data did, the same sequencing that later became the Current State and Operating Model phases of the Enterprise AI Blueprint.

bullets: Engaged stakeholders to define business requirements, clarify use cases, and establish success metrics for the deployment.

Platform fully integrated and operational, with engineers using it to collect customer asset vibration data and improve uptime and operational safety.

sqdc.safety: Earlier detection of equipment issues in the field
sqdc.quality: Proper governance, training, and user adoption from day one
sqdc.cost: Avoided wasted software investment through disciplined deployment

enterpriseProjects.challenge: An externally purchased predictive maintenance product needed to move from purchase to real production impact.
outcomes: Coordinated 6+ cross-functional teams to deliver into production
Gave engineers live visibility into customer asset health
Avoided wasted software spend by ensuring proper deployment and adoption
enterpriseProjects.executiveSummary: GE Power had already purchased a predictive maintenance platform. The harder problem was making it actually operational, integrated, adopted, and trusted enough that engineers used it to make real maintenance calls rather than letting the investment sit unused.
enterpriseProjects.businessChallenge: Vendor software purchases routinely stall between procurement and production, especially when they require coordination across cloud, security, and architecture teams who weren't part of the original buying decision. The risk here wasn't technical failure, it was the far more common failure of a good tool never reaching the people who needed to use it.
enterpriseProjects.myRole: I led the deployment as the single point of accountability across six-plus cross-functional teams, translating a vendor relationship into an internally adopted capability. That meant defining the requirements the vendor needed to meet, sequencing the technical rollout, and personally ensuring the platform reached the engineers who would rely on it.

Coordinated vendor, cloud, security, and architecture teams around a single delivery plan.
Built and delivered the training that made adoption possible from day one.
enterpriseProjects.blueprintConnection: This is where I saw firsthand that a good tool with no adoption plan is just an expensive shelf item. That distinction, between deploying technology and operationalizing a capability, is the difference the Enterprise AI Blueprint is built to address for AI initiatives specifically.

Developed training and adoption support to ensure teams could use the new system from day one.
Successfully replaced the legacy system with knowledge continuity preserved, operational disruption avoided, and adoption increased.

sqdc.quality: Solution aligned with user needs through stakeholder-led requirements
sqdc.delivery: Smooth phased rollout with minimal disruption

enterpriseProjects.challenge: A failing legacy knowledge system put critical engineering documentation at risk.

Phased rollout minimized disruption to engineering teams
Adoption support had teams productive on the new platform from day one
enterpriseProjects.executiveSummary: A failing Lotus Notes knowledge system put years of engineering documentation at risk of becoming inaccessible. This initiative replaced the platform without losing the knowledge it held or disrupting the engineering teams who depended on it daily.
enterpriseProjects.businessChallenge: The system was end-of-life and increasingly unstable, but it also held institutional knowledge accumulated over years, with no clean way to migrate it. Any misstep risked either losing critical documentation or disrupting engineering teams who had no tolerance for downtime.
enterpriseProjects.myRole: I owned the platform decision and the migration strategy, from evaluating alternatives through to leading the technical migration and the adoption plan that came with it. The harder part wasn't the technology choice, it was designing a rollout that protected continuity for teams who couldn't afford to lose access to their own documentation.

Led the technical migration, including data extraction, cleaning, and deployment.
enterpriseProjects.blueprintConnection: This project reinforced that migrations succeed or fail on adoption, not technology, a lesson that shows up directly in the Blueprint's treatment of adoption and change enablement as a distinct phase, not an afterthought bolted onto delivery.

enterpriseProjects.executiveSummary: Aging SharePoint infrastructure had become a real operational and security exposure. This initiative upgraded the platform through a carefully sequenced cutover that protected data integrity for a global user base.
enterpriseProjects.businessChallenge: The platform was out of support and increasingly risky to run, but it was also in active use by a large global population, meaning any upgrade had to be executed with zero tolerance for data loss and minimal tolerance for downtime.
enterpriseProjects.myRole: I owned the risk framework and the cutover strategy, including the judgment call, mid-execution, to pause the go-live when early signals suggested a problem, rather than push through on schedule. That decision protected the outcome at the cost of the original timeline.

hero.headline: From Enterprise Technology to Enterprise AI
narrative: Over two decades leading enterprise technology initiatives, I discovered that organizations rarely struggle because of technology alone. They struggle because governance, operating models, leadership, and adoption aren't connected. That realization ultimately led me to focus on how organizations operationalize Enterprise AI.
AI didn't introduce a new category of organizational failure. It exposed the same one, at a larger scale, moving faster, with less room to recover from getting it wrong.

leadership.label: ENTERPRISE LEADERSHIP
leadership.headline: Twenty years building the systems that determine whether technology investments actually work.
leadership.body: Product management, portfolio management, governance, decision support, and modernization, at executive scale, across GE Vernova, GE Power, Pratt & Whitney, and Alstom Power. That experience isn't the credential. It's the foundation the rest of this perspective is built on.

whyAI.label: WHY ENTERPRISE AI
whyAI.headline: The hardest problems were never really about the technology.
body: The deeper I got into enterprise technology leadership, the more I noticed that the hardest problems came down to whether an organization could govern a decision, build an operating model people would actually use, and get people to adopt a change instead of quietly working around it.

Enterprise AI didn't change that pattern. It raised the stakes on it. The organizations that succeed with AI won't be the ones with the best models, they'll be the ones who can operationalize it the way they'd operationalize any enterprise capability: with governance, ownership, adoption, and a way to measure whether it's actually working.

That's the problem I became interested in solving, not AI as a technology, but AI as something an organization has to be built to sustain. That interest is what eventually became the Enterprise AI Blueprint.

applied.label: BUILDING APPLIED AI
applied.headline: Testing the thinking by building it.
applied.body: My applied AI products demonstrate how these ideas translate into working software.

reflection.label: WHAT CHANGED
reflection.quote: Organizations rarely struggle because of the technology itself. They struggle because governance, operating models, product leadership, adoption, and business alignment were never connected to begin with, each one solved in isolation, if it gets solved at all. That realization became the foundation for everything I've built since.

lookingAhead.label: LOOKING AHEAD
lookingAhead.headline: Where I'm focused now.
lookingAhead.body: Helping organizations move from AI experimentation to a governed, scalable, measurable enterprise capability, the same disciplines that made a difference long before AI was the assignment, applied to the one in front of us now.

about.closing: Enterprise AI isn't just another technology shift. It's an organizational transformation. My work today is focused on helping organizations build the structures, governance, and leadership needed to make Enterprise AI a lasting business capability.
about.emotionalClose: Enterprise AI isn't the destination for me, it became the natural evolution of everything I'd spent my career solving. The technology changed. The organizational challenges did not.

pov.headline: My Point of View on Enterprise AI
pov.body: Most organizations are not failing at AI because of the models. They are struggling because they are applying AI to problems that have not been translated into clear, actionable decisions. AI does not solve problems directly. It supports decisions that address those problems. If the decision is not clearly defined, owned, and measurable, AI introduces risk instead of value.
pov.coreInsight: I view AI as a decision-support capability, not a decision-maker. The decision must be explicit, ownership must be assigned, and outcomes must be measurable and validated.
approach: Start with the decision: define what needs to be decided, who owns it, and what success looks like
Separate pattern work from judgment: AI supports pattern recognition, humans own tradeoffs
Keep AI in an advisory role with required human validation
Track false positives, false negatives, and business impact
Assign ownership and monitor outcomes through feedback loops

productApproach.title: Start with the Decision
productApproach.body: I define the decision we are trying to improve, who owns it, and what action it drives. If the decision is unclear, I do not move forward.

productApproach.title: Decompose the Workflow
productApproach.body: I map the end-to-end workflow, separating data retrieval, rules-based logic, pattern recognition, and human judgment to identify where AI actually fits.

productApproach.title: Choose the Right Approach
productApproach.body: I determine whether the problem requires rules, search, retrieval-based approaches, or machine learning. Not every problem needs AI.

productApproach.title: Design Human + AI Interaction
productApproach.body: I define what the AI does, what the human does, and where validation occurs. AI supports decisions, but humans remain accountable.

productApproach.title: Define Success & Risk
productApproach.body: I establish business metrics and assess risk early, ensuring outputs are measurable, reversible, and appropriate for the level of impact.

productApproach.title: Pilot, Measure, and Scale
productApproach.body: I start with a narrow use case, measure both output quality and workflow impact, and scale only when value, trust, and control are proven.

hero.headline: Helping organizations operationalize Enterprise AI as a governed, scalable, and measurable business capability.
body: Most organizations can launch AI pilots. Far fewer can operationalize Enterprise AI across the business because operationalization requires more than technology. It requires governance, operating models, product leadership, adoption, and the organizational capabilities needed to sustain AI at enterprise scale.

Over more than two decades of enterprise technology leadership, including product strategy, governance, and application portfolio management at GE Vernova, I helped organizations make better technology investment decisions, contributing to a 50% improvement in portfolio health and a 40% reduction in portfolio size.

Building on that experience, I developed the Enterprise AI Blueprint, a structured executive methodology that helps organizations assess AI readiness, identify capability gaps, design an operating model, and operationalize Enterprise AI responsibly and at scale.

blueprint.label: STRUCTURED METHODOLOGY
blueprint.headline: The Enterprise AI Blueprint
body: The Enterprise AI Blueprint is a structured executive methodology I developed to help organizations understand their current position, assess readiness, identify capability gaps, establish an operating model, operationalize AI, and connect implementation to measurable business outcomes.

It draws on more than two decades of enterprise technology leadership, recent applied AI product work, and focused research into how organizations move AI from experimentation to sustained enterprise capability.

hero.headline: The Enterprise AI Blueprint
body: The Enterprise AI Blueprint is a structured executive framework for moving Enterprise AI from isolated pilots to a governed, scalable, and measurable business capability.

The Enterprise AI Blueprint emerged from a simple observation: the organizational disciplines that determine whether enterprise technology succeeds also determine whether Enterprise AI succeeds. Governance, product leadership, operating models, adoption, and value realization are not AI-specific. They are enterprise capabilities that become even more critical as organizations operationalize AI.
That perspective was shaped through more than two decades of enterprise product management, governance, and technology investment leadership across large enterprise organizations.

struggle.label: WHY ORGANIZATIONS STRUGGLE
struggle.headline: Launching an AI pilot is often the easy part. Building the governance, operating model, and organizational capabilities required to sustain AI as an enterprise capability is much harder.
struggle.intro: Pilots are relatively easy to fund and easy to demo. What's difficult is everything after the demo: governance that holds up under real use, delivery that survives contact with existing systems, adoption that outlasts the initial enthusiasm, and a way to prove the investment was worth it. Most AI initiatives don't fail because the model was wrong. They stall because the organization never built the capability to run them at scale.

patterns.title: Treated as a project, not a capability
patterns.body: The pilot succeeds, then ends, because there was never a plan to operate it as an ongoing part of the business.

patterns.title: Governance added after the fact
patterns.body: Oversight gets bolted on once something goes wrong, instead of being designed into the initiative from the start.

patterns.title: Adoption left to chance
patterns.body: The tool is deployed, but no one owns whether people actually change how they work because of it.

steps.label: THE SIX-STEP BLUEPRINT
steps.headline: A structured path from fragmented activity to operational AI capability.
steps.intro: Each phase answers a specific executive question. Together, they move an organization from uncertainty about where it stands to a governed capability it can measure and sustain.

howItWorks.label: HOW THE BLUEPRINT WORKS
howItWorks.headline: Each phase builds on the one before it.
body: The Blueprint is sequential, not because process demands it, but because each phase produces something the next phase depends on. You cannot design a credible operating model before you understand your actual readiness. You cannot operationalize AI at scale on top of a governance structure that doesn't yet exist.

In practice, the phases are iterative. Organizations revisit earlier phases as conditions change, new initiatives emerge, or readiness gaps close. What stays constant is the discipline of not skipping ahead. Most of the AI initiatives that stall did so because a later-stage problem, usually adoption or governance, was never addressed at the stage where it needed to be.

relationship.label: RELATIONSHIP TO ENTERPRISE AI
relationship.headline: The Blueprint connects the disciplines that operationalizing AI actually requires.
relationship.body: Enterprise AI is not one initiative or one technology decision. It is the product of several disciplines operating as a single system, and the Blueprint is the structure that connects them.

closing.headline: Ready to operationalize Enterprise AI?
closing.body: The Blueprint is the framework. The conversation is where it gets specific to your organization's current state, constraints, and goals.
